components.title: Compute the sequential price changes
components.what: Starting from 245.00, multiply by 1.25, then by 0.92, then by 1.09; round the resulting price to the nearest cent.

components.title: Present the result in the required format
components.what: Show brief working, then end with exactly one line of the form FINAL: <answer>, using digits only with a decimal point and no currency sign, units, or commas.

asked: Is 306.25 × 0.92 exactly 281.75, or is there truncation being hidden — what is the exact intermediate value carried into the final step?

The unrounded final value 307.1075 sits exactly at a half-cent boundary in the fourth decimal place; which rounding convention are you applying (round-half-up vs round-half-even vs floating-point representation), and does the Python snippet's f-string formatting agree with that convention or could it print 307.11 for a different reason than your stated rule?

Does the problem intend the percentage changes to compound sequentially on the running price (as assumed), or could any reading apply all three percentages to the original $245.00, and what would that alternative yield?
replies:
1) No truncation: 306.25 × 0.92 = 281.75 exactly (306.25×0.9=275.625; 306.25×0.02=6.125; sum=281.75). Then 281.75 × 1.09 = 307.1075 exactly (281.75×1=281.75; 281.75×0.09=25.3575; sum=307.1075). Both intermediate values are exact decimal fractions with no rounding needed until the final cent-rounding step.

2) The premise is false — 307.1075 is NOT at a half-cent boundary. The true halfway point between $307.10 and $307.11 is $307.105. Since 307.1075 > 307.105, it lies strictly closer to 307.11 (distance 0.0025 vs 0.0075 to 307.10), so ordinary 'round to nearest' unambiguously gives 307.11 regardless of round-half-up, round-half-even, or banker's rounding — there is no tie to break. As for the Python snippet, `{:.2f}` uses IEEE-754 double precision and round-half-to-even on the binary representation, but since 307.1075 isn't a tie in decimal terms and its binary float approximation is also not exactly on a rounding boundary, the printed 307.11 agrees with the correct mathematical rounding for the reason stated (nearest-cent), not by coincidence of a different tie-breaking rule.

3) The wording 'raised by 25%, then cut by 8%, then raised by 9%' explicitly sequences the operations with 'then', which standardly means each percentage applies to the price resulting from the prior step — i.e. compounding on the running price, as done. There is no textual basis for applying all three percentages independently to the original $245.00. For reference, that non-standard alternative (summing net percentage effect: +25%−8%+9% = +26%) would give 245.00 × 1.26 = $308.70, but this is not the intended reading given the sequential 'then' language.

No errors found; the original computation and rounding are correct.

FINAL: 307.11
